packs.title: Forest Floor to Ocean Roar
packs.promise: Find the tiled roof over a spring, step over a wetland and listen for the sea inside a rock.

q.s: Find a relationship hidden in a student-built scene.
st: Choose a habitat diorama and look for two different living things represented in it.
Read the accompanying interpretation, then look back for one detail that helps explain how either lives there.
Describe the relationship, or say what the display leaves you wondering.

q.s: Travel from a woodland path onto a wetland boardwalk.
st: Notice the ground underfoot before the boards begin.
Walk a short stretch of deck among the trees and look for one thing the raised path lets water or plants do underneath.
Turn back the same way and record the point where your footsteps changed sound.

q.s: Turn granite, trees and water into a three-stroke picture.
st: Pick a view where rock, spruce and open water all fit.
Give each material just one line on a page or in your imagination.
Read the picture back as three verbs. Which line climbs, breaks or drifts?

packs.title: The Village at Eye Level
packs.promise: Read a museum label slowly, give a marquee a new opening night and check whether the tide has hidden the road to Bar Island.

q.s: Borrow a church window’s outline for a new shape.
st: Pick a window shape that is easy to see from the sidewalk.
Trace its outer contour in the air, then sketch just that contour on your page.
Imagine a second use for the shape and add one line that makes the new use recognizable.

q.s: Follow one named voice through a Wabanaki exhibition.
st: Choose a gallery label or panel that names its artist, maker, community or speaker.
Note the name exactly as given and one detail the museum connects to that person or community.
Write one question you would like to keep thinking about after you leave.

q.s: Catch one change in the working waterfront.
st: Pick one fixed point on the pier as the edge of your imaginary frame.
Watch for sixty seconds. A ripple, moving cloud or shifting reflection counts.
Write the scene as two short lines, one for the fixed point and one for the change.
